This criminal original petition has been filed to quash the proceedings in S.M.M.F.No.21 of 2011 pending on the file of the XX http://www.judis.nic.in Metropolitan Magistrate Court, Egmore,
Chennai.

2.The petitioner is the manufacturer of coffee powder under the brand name styled as "Leo Coffee"
and this product is being manufactured under license in its factory premises situated at No.16,
South Mada Street, Mylapore, Chennai-600 004.

sentences.text: 3.The facts of the case is that the respondent took three samples of LEO Coffee Powder Packets weighing 200 grams from the premises of MORE Departmental Store, situated at 24/1, Dr.Nair Road, T.Nagar, Chennai-600 017.
The above samples were sent for analysis on 04.12.2009 to the Public Analyst, Corporation of Chennai who in turn reported that "the sample is found to be misbranded".

On the basis of the Public Analyst Report dated 08.01.2010, the respondent filed charge sheet dated 30.05.2010 arraying the petitioner as A-3 along with two other accused, who were the sales personnel of M/s.More Departmental Store arraying them as A-1 and A-2.
http://www.judis.nic.in 4.Thereafter, on 28.06.2011 notice was issued to the petitioner calling for explanation for the alleged contravention under Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act 1954, for having manufactured and sold misbranded product.

Though the alleged samples were taken as early as on 04.12.2009 and the public analysts report was received as early as on 08.01.2010, notice was issued under Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act 1954 only on 28.06.2011, after delay of 18 months.
The public analysts report dated 08.01.2010 should have been served on the petitioner immediately within a reasonable time, but after the shelf life of the food product, notice has been served.
The respondent filed a compliant in the year 2011, when the product had lost its shelf life which is against the statue.
However, the respondent filed a complaint before the learned XX Metropolitan Magistrate, Egmore in S.M.M.F No.21 of 2011.
Challenging the same, this criminal original petition is filed.

5.The learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that the respondent took three samples of LEO Coffee Powder packets weighing 200 grams, from the premises of M/s.More Departmental Store, situated http://www.judis.nic.in at 24/1, Dr.Nair Road, T.Nagar, Chennai-600 017 on 04.12.2009 and sent the same for analysis on 04.12.2009 to the Public Analyst, Corporation of Chennai, who in turn sent the report on 08.01.2010.

It is the submission of the learned counsel for the petitioner that the date of manufacture of LEO Coffee powder packet is November 2009 and the expiry of the product is within 9 months from the date of packaging.
The complaint was filed before the learned Magistrate only in the year 2011, after expiry of the shelf life of the product.
Therefore, it is the submission of the learned counsel for the petitioner that the product had lost its shelf life, at the time when the product was being analysed.

The learned counsel further submits that the petitioner was not given opportunity by providing the report of the public analyst before the expiry of shelf life of the product and thereby, he had lost his valuable right for sending the same for second analysis and therefore, the prosecution launched by the respondent is not sustainable in the eye of law.
6.On the above contentions, this Court heard the learned Government Advocate (Crl. Side) and perused the materials available on http://www.judis.nic.in record.
7. The facts in the present case as to the seizure of the product, sending the same for public analyst report and the further acton taken on the said report are not in dispute.

sentences.text:
The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Alkem Laboratories Limited  Vs - State of Madhya Pradesh [2019] 0 Supreme (C) 1310 dealing on the procedure to be followed by the authorities to prove a product as a misbranded one, held as under:-
"The question which arises then is, what is the procedure to be followed in cases where proving misbranding requires testing of the relevant food samples, but the corresponding charge of adulteration has not been made.

entities.text: Alkem Laboratories Limited  Vs - State of Madhya Pradesh [2019] 0 Supreme (C) 1310
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Section 13(2) is unfortunately silent in this regard.
It is a settled principle of statutory interpretation that any ambiguity in a penal statute has to be interpreted in favour of the accused.

It would be absurd and discriminatory for the prosecution to, on one hand, rely on the report of the Public Analyst under Section 13(1) for proving the offence of misbranding, http://www.judis.nic.in and on the other hand, claim that the accused cannot avail of their right to challenge the said report as per Sections 13(2) and 13(3)
because it is not a case of adulteration.

In such a scenario, the word adulterated in Section 13(2) would have to be read as including misbranded in so far as it relates to the ingredients of the concerned food article, and the relevant clauses of Section 13 have to be complied with in their entirety."
9.
In the case on hand, the sample of the product was taken on 04.12.2009 and was sent for analysis on the same day on 04.12.2009.
However, the Public Analyst, Corporation of Chennai, sent the report only on 08.01.2010.

A notice under Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act,
1954 was issued to the petitioner after lapse of 18 months on 28.06.2011.
10.The

test report of the analyst was given on 08.01.2010 and the complaint was filed before the learned Magistrate 30.05.2011, i.e., almost at or about the time, the product was about to lose its shelf life.

A perusal of the record reveals that the petitioner was not given an http://www.judis.nic.in opportunity, before the expiry of the shelf life of the product, for reanalysing the product, which had robbed the petitioner of his valuable right to have the product analysed for a second time.
The decision relied on by the learned counsel for the petitioner is squarely attracted to the case on hand.

11.In view of all the above and taking note of the delay in launching the prosecution, I am of the opinion that the prosecution launched against the petitioner/A3 is wholly unsustainable not only on account of the belated prosecution initiated against the petitioner, which has robbed his right to have the product reanalysed, but also for violation of principles of natural justice, as the petitioner was not provided with an opportunity at the earliest point of time, by giving a copy of the report of the analyst, which would have allowed him to take recourse in accordance with law.
The act of the respondents had resulted in the petitioner losing his valuable right for sending the sample for second analysis.
http://www.judis.nic.in 12.For the reasons aforesaid, this Court has no hesitation to allow the present petition.

Accordingly,
this criminal original petition is allowed and the proceedings in S.M.M.F.No.21 of 2011 on the file of the XX Metropolitan Magistrate Court, Chennai is hereby quashed against the petitioner/A3 alone.
